moat_against: Sherwin-Williams stronger in US architectural; PPG exited US/Canada architectural coatings
Raw-material cost pass-through lags — 2022 OE collapsed
Cyclical end markets: auto builds, housing, industrial production
Low-single-digit long-run growth; AkzoNobel/Axalta/regional rivals contest every segment
moat_for: Top-tier global scale with broad distribution incl. Comex network in Mexico
Qualification/technical-service switching costs in aerospace and auto OEM/refinish coatings
Demonstrated pricing power through raw-material cycles
Diversified end markets cushion single-cycle downturns
moat_justification: Moderate, not wide: top-tier global scale alongside Sherwin-Williams/AkzoNobel, qualification and technical-service switching costs in aerospace and automotive OEM/refinish coatings, and demonstrated pricing power (+2% price in Q2 2026 after the 2022-23 pass-through cycle). Against that, Sherwin-Williams holds the stronger US architectural position and PPG exited US/Canada architectural coatings, raw-material costs (resins, TiO2) are passed through only with a lag (2022 conservative OE fell to $443M), end markets are cyclical, and long-run revenue growth is low-single-digit (3y CAGR 0.55%). CAP = 8.5 years.
name: PPG Industries, Inc.
one_liner: Moderate-moat (5/10) global coatings leader, but at $107.50 owner's earnings clear only 7.8% weighted — IV@15% $45.43, and even the super-bull case ($86.96) sits below the price; it would need to fall to ~$45 to clear the 15% hurdle.
